newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs lightly trade $1.00 lower-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs lightly trade $1.00 lower-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog markets were slow to develop Friday and the few early trades were mostly $1.00 per cwt lower, livestock dealers said.

Meat packers have Friday's and most of Monday's slaughter needs filled and were not pressed to bid for hogs early. Saturday's slaughter was expected to be light, with poor operating margins discouraging the extra shift.

Interior Iowa-southern Minnesota hogs traded from $52.00 to $52.50 at country points and $53.00 to $53.50 delivered to plants. Illinois sources reported early steady to lower trades of $52.00 to $52.50 at country points and $53.50 at plants.
Hog marketings were light in nearly all Midwest markets because producers anticipated the lower prices, sources said.
Cash pork prices fell sharply through midweek, but stabilized somewhat late Thursday.
USDA reported pork cutout values were unchanged to down $0.01 per cwt late Thursday.
